test_title: PYST 37: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The Right to Protection in respect of conviction for offences (including protection from double jeopardy and self-incrimination) is covered under:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 20**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 20** of the **Indian Constitution** provides protection in respect of conviction for offenses and includes provisions against **double jeopardy** and **self-incrimination**.
 
• **Clause (1): Protection against ex-post facto laws:** No person shall be convicted of any offense except for the violation of a law that was in force at the time of the commission of the act. This means that laws cannot be applied retrospectively to penalize actions that were legal at the time they were committed. *Correct statement.*
 
• **Clause (2): Protection against double jeopardy:** No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offense more than once. This ensures that individuals cannot face repeated trials or penalties for the same offense, maintaining fairness in the legal process. *Correct statement.*
 
• **Clause (3): Protection against self-incrimination:** No person accused of any offense shall be compelled to be a witness against themselves. This clause secures the fundamental right to silence and prevents forced confessions or self-incriminating evidence. *Correct statement.*
 
• **Scope and applicability:** Article 20 applies to criminal offenses and protects individuals from unjust legal practices. It is considered one of the essential provisions safeguarding personal liberty and fairness in legal proceedings.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Article 20.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 22:**

 
 
• **deals with protection against arbitrary arrest and detention. It guarantees rights such as being informed of the grounds of arrest, the right to consult a lawyer, and being presented before a magistrate within 24 hours of arrest.
 
• It also provides for preventive detention but sets limits on its duration and safeguards against its misuse.
 
 
 
• Article 23:**
 
 
• **prohibits human trafficking, forced labor, and begar (compulsory unpaid labor). It protects individuals from exploitation and ensures dignity in labor.
 
• However, the Constitution allows the state to impose compulsory service for public purposes, provided it does not discriminate on grounds like religion or caste.
 
 
 
• Article 21:**
 
 
• **guarantees the protection of life and personal liberty. It ensures that no person is deprived of their life or liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
 
• It is a broad provision and encompasses rights such as the right to privacy, the right to a dignified life, and the right to health, among others.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Double Jeopardy:**

 
 
• Double jeopardy is derived from **Article 20(2)**. It protects individuals from being punished twice for the same offense.
 
• This principle is also recognized internationally under the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948).
 
 
 
• **Self-Incrimination:**
 
 
• The protection against self-incrimination under **Article 20(3)** is similar to the Fifth Amendment of the United States Constitution.
 
• This provision ensures that individuals are not forced to provide evidence against themselves during legal proceedings, preserving fairness and justice.
 
 
 
• **Ex-post facto laws:**
 
 
• The prohibition against ex-post facto laws under **Article 20(1)** ensures that individuals cannot be penalized retroactively for actions that were not illegal at the time they were committed.
 
• However, this protection applies only to criminal laws and not civil laws.
